name: Chhatu Rai
subtitle: mushrooms simmered in a hot mustard and poppy seed gravy, a monsoon favourite

ingredients.note: the closest stand-in for wild monsoon chhatu

prepNotes: Soak the mustard seeds and poppy seeds together in warm water for 20 minutes, then grind with 2 green chillies and 3 tbsp water into a fine paste.
Wipe the mushrooms with a damp cloth instead of washing them; soaked mushrooms leak water and refuse to brown.
Crush the garlic and ginger to a coarse paste in a mortar rather than a blender. You want texture in this gravy.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes lightly, then lower to medium-high.
Add the mushrooms with 1/2 tsp salt and fry hard for 6 to 7 minutes, without stirring much, until they have given up their water and the edges are browned.
steps.tip: Wait through the wet stage. Mushrooms boil in their own liquid first and only brown after it evaporates.

steps.text: Scoop the mushrooms out and set aside, leaving the oil in the pan.
Crackle the panch-phoron in the same oil for 20 seconds until it pops and smells nutty.
Add the crushed garlic and ginger and fry for 2 minutes until the raw edge goes and the paste turns straw coloured.
Stir in the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and cumin powder and cook for 5 minutes, pressing with the spoon, until the tomato breaks down and oil beads at the sides.
steps.tip: That ring of separated oil is the signal the masala is done. Rush it and the gravy tastes raw.

steps.text: Return the mushrooms, pour in the water, and simmer uncovered for 6 minutes.
Drop the heat to its lowest, stir in the mustard-poppy paste and the remaining slit green chilli, and cook 4 minutes at a bare simmer.
steps.tip: Do not boil after the mustard goes in. It turns bitter fast and never comes back.

steps.text: Taste for salt, take off the heat and finish with the coriander and a teaspoon of raw mustard oil.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat on low heat only, adding a splash of water; a hard reboil will make the mustard bitter.
